source.title: Enhancing Accuracy in Deep Learning Using Random Matrix Theory
source.authors: Leonid Berlyand; E. Sandier; Yitzchak Shmalo; Lei Zhang

record.file_problem: Text is complete and readable, though it contains OCR/encoding artifacts.
record.tranche_reason: The study trains large networks from random initialization and reports training accuracy on CIFAR-10, but its intervention includes RMT pruning and the relevant CIFAR-10 training-accuracy results are shown only in a figure.
record.gate_note: CIFAR-10 training-accuracy results appear in Figure 10 without numerical values or a textual description of whether training error approaches zero. Other reported outcomes, including test accuracy and parameter counts, do not measure the version's training-error claim. Initialization comparisons do not report the training-speed or trainable-depth outcomes named in V4.
record.test_reason: The unpruned comparator trains a randomly initialized CNN on CIFAR-10 and measures training classification accuracy, matching V1's method and measure. Figure 10 also reports the pruned model's training accuracy, but neither outcome is readable from the supplied text.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the CIFAR-10 comparison and the lack of a readable training-error endpoint. The broader author conclusion is that MP-based pruning reduces parameters while preserving roughly comparable CNN accuracy and improving fully connected network accuracy and variability across initializations. They interpret lower training losses as evidence of a simpler loss landscape and provide conditional accuracy-preservation theorems; these results do not directly verify avoidance of spurious local minima.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses MP-based singular-value pruning during training; its unpruned comparator is normally trained. CIFAR-10 networks use batch normalization, dropout, L2 regularization, momentum, and a decaying learning rate.
record.method_sensitivity: The study reports that CIFAR-10 pruning reduces parameter count and that accuracy is slightly lower for the pruned network; it does not describe how training accuracy changes across conditions.

fits_no_version.finding: Fully connected MNIST and Fashion MNIST networks achieve lower training loss and higher training accuracy with MP-based pruning; a Fashion MNIST run reaches 100% training accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: MP-based pruning can improve training fit in the tested fully connected image classifiers. These architectures and datasets fall outside V1, and the results do not establish V2's teacher-student local-minimum claim.

fits_no_version.finding: The normally trained CNN reaches 100% training accuracy on MNIST and approximately 99% on Fashion MNIST; pruned CNNs have lower training accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Large CNNs can fit the tested MNIST and Fashion MNIST training sets closely, with pruning reducing training fit.

record.problems: The relevant CIFAR-10 training-accuracy results are presented only in Figure 10, with no numerical values or textual description of training error. The text reports five seeds but does not give uncertainty values for this result.
record.rows_left_out: No additional results bearing on V1 were reported in text or tables. Test accuracy and parameter-count results were left out because they do not measure training error.

untested.parts: CIFAR-100, corrupted or random labels, systematic model-size comparisons, early stopping, and comparisons isolating regularization. The CIFAR-10 training-error endpoint is measured but unreadable in the supplied text.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems, verified spurious local minima, and adding one or two student neurons.
Depth-dependent degradation and controlled comparisons of plain networks with identity shortcuts.

Effects of initialization on training speed or trainable depth, signal and gradient propagation, and orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization. The initialization experiments describe accuracy and pruning compatibility without establishing these effects.
Learning rates relative to a measured stability threshold, curvature trajectories, catapult recovery, and edge-of-stability dynamics.
Controlled normalization comparisons, learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup. Using batch normalization alone does not test its benefits.

record.verdict_notes: No verdict label is justified for V1 because neither linked row establishes the training-error endpoint. Figure-only reporting is an evidence limitation, not a scope-limiting result. The study is not an original source for any listed version.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-100, corrupted or random labels, smaller models, early stopping, and the stated regularized recipes.
